data.name: Home_Intro
data.value: Antimicrobial resistance data for the laboratory, shared from one reference spreadsheet. Every reader sees the same file.

data.value: The ranking is per organism: it lists what that one species is least susceptible to, most resistant first. Drugs this report never tested against the organism carry no percentage and are listed after the measured ones. Type any part of the name — "aureus" finds every Staphylococcus aureus — then choose it from the list.

data.name: Mappings_IntroFirst
data.value: Each antibiotic abbreviation this file uses is listed below, in the order the file lists it. Fill in the meaning next to the names that need one and save them all at once. Nothing is pre-decided: the meanings are recorded by the pathologists, and they belong to this file alone. The same abbreviation can mean a different drug in a different file.

data.value: A file that already spells its antibiotics out in full needs no mapping at all, and this page will say so rather than asking for work that is not required.

data.name: Mappings_NotApplicableBody
data.value: Every antibiotic in it is already listed under its full name, so there is no abbreviation for a pathologist to interpret. This page only has work to do when a file names its antibiotics in short form, such as AMK %S.

data.name: Mappings_EditorHelp
data.value: Fill in any empty box with the full drug name, then press Save mappings. A meaning you want to remove is removed with its Remove button, not by clearing the box.
